objectClass.notes: The admitted front, side, front-three-quarter, and rear-three-quarter views describe one stylized classic rear-engine coupe. Geometry should match the concept sheet rather than claim manufacturing accuracy or use trademarked badges.

reasoning: The identity depends on a compound side silhouette: long low hood, upright windshield, near-flat roof crown, and continuous fastback rear arc.
Front and rear wheel openings must be carved negative spaces with painted arch lips; placing wheels against an uncut body is a reference-breaking shortcut.
The front view requires a wide low stance, exposed round headlamps embedded in raised fender crowns, a narrow black bumper strip, and small amber indicators.
The rear view requires a full-width dark red lamp band, horizontal engine grille, black bumper guards, and a single left exhaust outlet.
Five-spoke wheel repetition, separate wheel pivots, and stable axle sockets are required for both visual identity and game animation.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex is required because the four-view identity depends on a continuous compound body surface, true wheel-arch negative spaces, a shaped glazed cabin, repeated wheel hardware, layered PBR materials, and action-ready wheel pivots.

details.description: Sharp studio highlights ride over a saturated red base coat on the hood, roof, fenders, and doors.
A shallow center valley and two faceted shoulder planes run from the cowl toward the front bumper.
Two round headlamps are embedded into raised painted fender crowns rather than floating in front of the body.
A narrow black impact strip spans the front bumper below the painted nose.
Small rectangular amber indicator lenses sit inside the front bumper near each corner.
The front tire occupies a real cut-out negative space with a red faceted arch lip following the upper tire.
The rear tire is enclosed by a separate flared painted arch with a smaller visible gap than the old model.
Each wheel exposes five thick silver spokes, a recessed dark barrel, and a circular center cap.
A thick charcoal frame outlines the trapezoidal windshield and separates it cleanly from the red A-pillars and roof.
The side glass terminates in a rounded triangular rear quarter window under the fastback arc.
A thin dark cutline follows the front edge, rocker, and curved rear edge of the long coupe door.
A small horizontal black handle sits high on the door behind the side mirror.
Closely spaced horizontal black slats fill a recessed grille below the rear window.
A segmented dark-red lamp band spans nearly the entire tail between black end bezels.
Two chunky black vertical guards project from the rear bumper strip.
A single dark circular exhaust outlet exits below the left side of the rear bumper.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the admitted side view the hood, windshield, roof, fastback, wheelbase, wheel diameter, and wheel-arch openings read as the same stylized coupe rather than a generic sports car.
At the admitted front view the wide low stance, fender crowns, inset round headlamps, bumper strip, and amber indicators align with the concept.
At the admitted rear three-quarter view the roof-to-tail arc, rear grille, full-width lamp band, bumper guards, and left exhaust are present and correctly layered.
Wheels expose five spokes and remain independently named pivot groups compatible with the existing game animation.
Automotive paint, glass, rubber, metallic wheels, black trim, and lamp lenses remain visually distinct under neutral and grazing light.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: The side profile explicitly controls hood height, windshield rake, roof crown, fastback falloff, tail height, wheelbase, overhangs, and ground clearance.
The front profile explicitly controls track width, fender crown height, hood valley, headlamp centers, and cabin taper.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Body shell, cabin/glazing, four wheel pivots, lighting, bumpers, rear grille, and interior are separate named branches.
Door seams, hood shut line, fender-to-bumper boundaries, and glass frames are explicit local features rather than painted suggestions.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Each wheel pivot attaches to a named axle socket with local center, rotation axis, overlap, and gap tolerance.
Mirrors, bumper guards, exhaust, headlamps, indicators, and rear grille attach to named body sockets with explicit local transforms.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: The red clear-coated body, smoked glass, tire rubber, silver spokes, black trim, lamp glass, and amber indicators have separate material contracts.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived red paint, charcoal glass, near-black trim, dark rubber, silver wheel, ivory headlamp, amber indicator, and dark-red tail-lamp palette.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
